author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: Staff can open a booked visit's correction form prefilled with its current date and description, and submit an amendment that updates the same visit in place — validated like booking (description required, date later than today) — without adding a further visit to the pet, then land back on the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a booked visit's correction shows the visit form carrying that visit's current date and description
Submitting a description and a date later than today updates the same visit in place and shows the owner's record
A successful correction leaves the pet's visit count unchanged — the existing visit is amended, not a new one added
A blank description is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again
A date of today or earlier is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, still out of scope)
notes: Reuses the existing pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template and its visit model attribute. GET and POST share the .../visits/{visitId}/edit URL. NG-5 narrowed in docs/prd.md on 2026-08-04 so that correcting date/description is in scope while cancellation remains a non-goal.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the owner feature package unchanged. The slice reuses two established patterns: visit-creation validation in VisitController.processNewVisitForm (@Valid Visit + the controller-level non-future-date check), and edit-in-place from PetController.updatePetDetails (resolve the existing entity by path id, copy the submitted fields onto it, save the aggregate root via OwnerRepository). No new module, pattern, integration, or dependency. The one genuine adjustment: the existing @ModelAttribute("visit") loadPetWithVisit unconditionally constructs a NEW Visit and calls pet.addVisit(visit); on the edit routes that both fails to prefill the form and would add a second visit to the pet, directly violating the unchanged-count criterion. loadPetWithVisit must therefore distinguish new vs edit by presence of the visitId path variable (the same required=false technique PetController.findPet uses for petId): with visitId present, return the existing Visit found on the pet WITHOUT calling addVisit; absent, keep today's create-and-add behavior. Resolving the existing visit needs a thin Pet.getVisit(Integer id) accessor mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) — the only new symbol. Owner remains the sole write path; save cascades the in-place edit through the owner-pet-visit graph (system-design.md Contracts, Persistence).
integration_points: loadPetWithVisit (@ModelAttribute "visit") gains a visitId path variable, required=false, and branches: new visit for the .../visits/new routes, existing visit (no addVisit) for the .../visits/{visitId}/edit routes
new GetMapping and PostMapping on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit; GET returns pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm prefilled, POST validates then saves
Pet.getVisit(Integer id) — new accessor over pet.getVisits(), returns null when absent, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer)
POST edit binds description/date onto the existing managed Visit instance (id stays disallowed via the existing setDisallowedFields("id","*.id")), then owners.save(owner) cascades — no new visit row

patterns.description: updatePetDetails: edit-in-place — resolve existing entity by id from the aggregate, copy fields, saveAndFlush(owner). The visit edit is structurally identical (copy date+description onto the resolved visit).

processNewVisitForm: the validation shape to reuse verbatim — @Valid (description @NotBlank) plus the explicit result.rejectValue("date","typeMismatch.visitDate") when the date is not after today; on result.hasErrors() re-render pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.
findPet: the required=false path-variable branch (new vs existing) to replicate in loadPetWithVisit for visitId.

risks.risk: loadPetWithVisit runs before every mapping in the controller; if it still calls pet.addVisit on the edit path, the pet gains a phantom visit and the unchanged-count criterion (test theCorrectionShouldNotAddAFurtherVisitToThePet) fails.
risks.mitigation: Branch on visitId presence and call addVisit ONLY on the new-visit path; on edit, return the instance from Pet.getVisit(visitId) untouched so binding mutates the already-attached visit.

risks.risk: Owner/pet/visit mismatch — a visitId in the URL that is not one of the addressed pet's visits. Pet.getVisit returns null; unguarded this NPEs or, worse, could be steered to edit a visit outside the addressed pet (an IDOR-flavoured path-tampering surface; note the app has no auth, so aggregate-scoped resolution IS the only boundary here).
risks.mitigation: Fail closed exactly as the existing owner-not-found / pet-not-found guards in loadPetWithVisit do: when getVisit(visitId) is null, throw IllegalArgumentException. This keeps every visit reachable only through owner->pet->visit and mirrors the owner-edit form/URL mismatch rejection already recorded in the threat model. Defined by the design; kept OUT of the PRD acceptance contract per the PRD expert. A guard test is recommended, not required.

risks.risk: Template reuse cosmetics: the submit button reads #{addVisit} ("Add Visit") and the Previous Visits table would list the visit being edited. Both are outside the requirement contract.
risks.mitigation: Acceptable under the product owner's explicit "reuse the template as-is" instruction; the h2 already branches on visit['new'] so an existing visit renders "Visit" not "New Visit". Leave the label unless a follow-up slice asks for it; do not expand scope here.

notes: Mismatch-boundary decision: the design DEFINES fail-closed behavior (throw IllegalArgumentException on a visitId not under the addressed pet) because the implementation must choose something when the lookup returns null — leaving it undefined invites an NPE or a cross-aggregate edit. This is a consequence of aggregate-scoped resolution, not a new requirement, so it stays out of the acceptance criteria (no PRD change); a guard test is a recommended addition. No durable-memory writes: this is an existing pattern reused, not evolved, and system-design.md is current-state/derived-from-code, so wiring REQ-VIS-003 into the Implements column for VisitController/Visit/Owner/Pet is post-merge doc-sync work, not a triage-time edit. No design-doc-autofix records present — autofix audit skipped. Scoping: single behavior, minor verdict, no ADR.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The @BeforeEach init() method was modified by this slice (new Visit seeding added), and six new test methods were added. All construct Owner, Pet, and Visit via direct constructors (new Owner(), new Pet(), new Visit()). The testing brief (§ Test Data Construction) mandates: 'A slice touching a test moves that test's construction behind a factory. A slice adding a test writes it behind one from the start.' Factory methods are required for all touched and new test construction.
findings.fix: Introduce private factory methods, e.g. createOwnerWithPet(), createSeedVisit(), or overloads, that wrap the direct constructor calls. Move all construction in init() and in any new test methods behind them.

findings.description: Several tier-1 values (values that directly affect expected outcomes and are asserted on) appear as bare, unnamed literals violating the three-tier data naming convention (§ Three-Tier Data Naming). Specific instances: the seed description 'Rabies shot' appears in init() and is asserted in theVisitCorrectionFormShouldBePrefilledWithTheVisitsCurrentDateAndDescription; the seed date LocalDate.now().plusDays(5) is likewise unnamed and asserted; the corrected description 'Follow-up examination' is repeated across three test methods without a named constant; LocalDate.now().plusDays(10) is repeated across three test methods without a named constant. Each of these values drives the test outcome and must carry a role-describing name so the reader can distinguish signal from scaffolding at a glance.
findings.fix: Declare named constants at class level, e.g. SEED_VISIT_DESCRIPTION = "Rabies shot", SEED_VISIT_DATE = LocalDate.now().plusDays(5) (or derive it at use-site from a named offset), CORRECTED_DESCRIPTION = "Follow-up examination", CORRECTED_DATE = LocalDate.now().plusDays(10). Replace each bare literal with its constant.

approved_aspects: theCorrectionShouldNotAddAFurtherVisitToThePet directly pins Edge Case 3 (unchanged visit count) with an assertThat hasSize(1) on the pet's visit collection after a successful POST — this is the load-bearing acceptance criterion and it is properly covered

theBookedVisitShouldBeUpdatedInPlaceWhenTheCorrectionIsValid verifies that the existing visit's fields are mutated in place by asserting on the in-memory object after the POST, confirming the 'amended, not replaced' invariant from a second angle

theCorrectionShouldFailWhenTheVisitDoesNotBelongToThePet covers the mismatch guard (visitId not owned by pet) and correctly accepts either a direct or wrapped IllegalArgumentException, handling both Spring MVC exception wrapping modes
All five new tests follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD naming school mandated for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward
OwnerRepository is mocked at the repository boundary (a system boundary), and MockMvc is used for the HTTP boundary — both are sanctioned mock points per the mocking policy
Pet coverage 100%, VisitController coverage 97% — well above the 80% line-coverage target
All 10 tests pass with 0 failures and 0 skips

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Pet.getVisit(Integer id) returns null on a miss rather than Optional<Visit>. The code-quality checklist requires Optional for nullable return values. The existing Owner.getPet methods carry the same debt (Owner.java:126, 144), so the fix must be applied consistently: return Optional<Visit> here and update the null-check call site in VisitController.loadPetWithVisit to use .orElseThrow().
findings.fix: Change the return type to Optional<Visit>, wrap the found visit in Optional.of(visit), and return Optional.empty() in the fall-through case. In VisitController.loadPetWithVisit replace the null-check block with pet.getVisit(visitId).orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException(...)).

findings.description: The inline comment embeds the PRD artifact identifier REQ-VIS-003 ('the unchanged-count rule of REQ-VIS-003'). Requirement IDs are internal pipeline artifacts that are opaque to a future reader who has only the source tree, and they may become stale if the PRD is renumbered. The business rule the comment is defending — that the existing visit is returned so form binding amends it rather than creating a duplicate — should be expressed in plain language without the identifier.
findings.fix: Rewrite the comment to describe the invariant in plain language, for example: 'Return the existing Visit so form binding amends it in place; creating a new Visit here would add a duplicate to the pet.'

findings.description: The string literal "Rabies shot" is hardcoded independently on line 76 (setup) and line 129 (assertion) with no shared constant. If the setup value is updated without the assertion, the prefill test silently degrades to a fixed-string check against the new value. Testing principles require expected values to be derived from inputs — the assertion should reference the same constant as the setup.
findings.fix: Extract a private static final String constant, e.g. INITIAL_VISIT_DESCRIPTION = "Rabies shot", and replace both occurrences.

approved_aspects: checkFormat passes — no formatting violations
@PathVariable(required = false) for the optional visitId is a clean Spring MVC idiom; the null check branches correctly into the new vs edit paths
loadPetWithVisit handles the missing-visit case with IllegalArgumentException consistent with the existing missing-owner and missing-pet patterns
New handlers (initUpdateVisitForm, processUpdateVisitForm) follow the same structural pattern as their booking counterparts and are each under 10 lines
Date validation in processUpdateVisitForm mirrors processNewVisitForm exactly — same error code, same guard
Javadoc on Pet.getVisit follows the established Owner.getPet template including the isNew() guard — structurally consistent
All four REQ-VIS-003 acceptance criteria are covered by tests: prefill, valid update, blank description, past date, and the unchanged-visit-count invariant

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: NG-5 was narrowed by a non-goal scope decision but no ADR was created. The Non-Goals section comment states 'A non-goal ADR records the path to each decision.' The inline dated-note records only the fact of the narrowing, not the decision path — what alternatives were considered, why correcting a visit moves in while cancellation stays out. The prd-authoring skill confirms the **ADR:** link is the required instrument for non-goal decisions; the PRD should carry a **ADR:** link pointing to the new ADR once it exists. No file dated 2026-08-04 appears in docs/adr/.

The inline dated-note reads 'since it reuses the booking form's validation without adding state'. The phrase 'reuses the booking form's validation' is mechanism language: it describes how validation is implemented rather than what the behavior is, and it would change meaning when switching to a different technology stack. Behavioral phrasing that stays on the what side: 'since the same validation rules that govern booking also govern the correction, without adding lifecycle state.' Confirm whether this wording should be made behavioral before the ADR is linked, or whether it can be addressed in the same pass that creates the ADR.
The REQ-VIS-003 narrative sentence is approximately 38 words, exceeding the 30-word maximum required by the writing standards.
findings.fix: Replace 'updating the same visit rather than adding another to the pet, and the same validation that governs booking governs the correction `[REQ-VIS-003]`.' with 'updating the same visit rather than adding another to the pet. The same validation that governs booking governs the correction `[REQ-VIS-003]`.'

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theBookedVisitShouldBeUpdatedInPlaceWhenTheCorrectionIsValid extracts the amended visit with this.pet.getVisits().iterator().next(), which is index-based access on a collection. The testing-principles.md checklist item 7 requires collection-aware assertions instead of index-based access. Beyond the checklist violation, the approach is semantically weaker than it could be: the load-bearing property is that the visit with id TEST_VISIT_ID was amended in place, not merely that the first element of the collection was amended. Pet.getVisit(TEST_VISIT_ID) exists in the production API (Pet.java:93) and resolves by identity. Use this.pet.getVisit(TEST_VISIT_ID).orElseThrow() to obtain the amended visit before asserting its fields. Class sweep: the only other instance of iterator().next() in the test tree is ValidatorTests.java:45, which is pre-existing debt outside the change set.
findings.fix: Replace `Visit amended = this.pet.getVisits().iterator().next();` with `Visit amended = this.pet.getVisit(TEST_VISIT_ID).orElseThrow();`. This ties the assertion to the visit by identity, directly expressing that the correct record was updated in place.
